effect: The kidneys returned more filtered water to the blood while still making urine, completing the remaining goal. Saving water and replacing it with a drink are different routes.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the two routes addressed the same problem differently.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using blood with the urinary system was most worthwhile because the result showed that conserving water still leaves urine to carry wastes away.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving drinking water to the blood vessel was clear, but the result only reported its placement, so it added little beyond the original picture.

surprise.text: The kidneys could return more water to the blood while still producing urine; I had not connected those two outcomes as clearly before.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: both matched a stated goal and the pictured routes. The water-saving signals were already supplied, though, so I did not explore how they worked.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter connected familiar body functions in a similarly clear way, though I would hope for more explanation than a placement confirmation.
